question: In order for Mateen to walk a kilometer (\(1000\) meters) in his rectangular backyard, he must walk the length \(25\) times or walk its perimeter \(10\) times. What is the area of Mateen’s backyard in square meters?
solution:
Walking the length \(25\) times covers \(1000\) meters, so one length is
\[
1000\div25=40\text{ meters}.
\]
Similarly, walking the perimeter \(10\) times covers \(1000\) meters, so the perimeter is \(1000\div10=100\) meters.

A rectangle has two equal lengths and two equal widths. The two lengths account for \(2\cdot40=80\) meters of the perimeter, leaving \(100-80=20\) meters for the two widths. Each width is therefore \(20\div2=10\) meters.

The area is length times width:
\[
40\cdot10=\boxed{400}\text{ square meters},
\]
choice C.
